figures.caption: FIG. 1. Representative examples of the free energy functional Flin under the assumption B(t) = δ(t). (A) With decreasing delay distribution coefficient of variability (CV), the free energy global minimum (purple and blue filled circles) becomes progressively deeper. Additional metastable minima also become more pronounced (open circle). A discontinuous transition occurs when the position of the global minimum crosses over to 0 with decreasing effective mean-field inverse temperature βMF. (B) Parameter space positions corresponding to functions in (A). The line represents the phase transition boundary. Panel shows only the transition within the equalweight semi-periodic ansatz discussed in Sec. IV B. It should not be read as the full three-regime mean-field phase diagram of Fig. 2A, which additionally includes the collapsed states analyzed in Sec. IV C.

FIG. 2. Comparison of mean-field predictions and Monte Carlo results. (A) Three-regime mean-field phase diagram obtained by combining the uniform, point-collapsed, and oscillatory-collapsed criteria discussed in Sec. IV. (B) maps of the second autocorrelation-peak prominence (B1) and spike-rate entropy (B2), computed from the final Monte Carlo state at each parameter point. The qualitative characteristics of phases and their relative location in parameter space are maintained. (C) final Monte Carlo state for uniform phase, spike train with links representing energy-contributing interactions (C1) and the corresponding spike rate distribution (C2), inset showing associated autocorrelation function. (D1-2) point-collapsed phase, sub-panels as above; note the ’glassy’ disordered internal structure of spike interactions qualitatively similar to Izhikevich’s neuronal groups (zoom panel D3). (E) oscillatory-collapsed phase, sub-panels as above, note the temporally ordered internal structure of spike interactions (zoom panel E3).
